title: introduce-runway-guardian-prefill-cli-and-telemetry-adapter
author: Eloise Chen
release_notes: Adds Runway Guardian CLI and telemetry adapter for tenant prefill policies; introduces compact quant profile generator and new default prefill templates. Backwards-compatible.
description:
Summary: Introduces Runway Guardian, a lightweight tenant-level agent (CLI + small runtime hooks) that synthesizes conservative prefill defaults, emits compact quantization profiles for downstream inference, and forwards cost/latency telemetry to Redwood Optimize. Motivation: customers frequently ask for conservative, turn-key defaults to avoid surprise overages during ramp or traffic spikes. Existing autotuners are powerful but require telemetry plumbing and orchestration; this change delivers a compact, opinionated CLI and telemetry adapter to plug into private or dedicated environments so teams can run safe prefill policies without heavy ops work.

What this PR does: 1) Adds a new CLI (runway-guardian) that can: generate tenant prefill templates (batch/caching targets and KV cache sizes), simulate runway (estimated unit-econ over 30/90/180 day horizons), and emit compact quant profiles (fp16/int8 suggestions with safety thresholds). 2) Adds a telemetry adapter service that ingests existing serving metrics and forwards normalized cost/latency signals to the Optimize pipeline for automated recommendations and alerting. 3) Ships a small policy-as-code library (YAML templates + validation) so security and platform teams can codify guardrails. 4) Adds end-to-end tests, docs, and Helm chart pieces for private installs.

Design notes and constraints: - Conservative defaults: generated profiles bias toward lower ms/token and higher fail-safe batch limits to prioritize user experience during ramp. - Compact quant profiles: output is intentionally small (JSON with <= 8 keys) so it can be embedded in tenant metadata and pushed with model manifests. - Simulation model: a simple stochastic runway estimator that consumes sample qps+dist and returns expected cost curves; not intended to replace full econ tooling but to give a conservative operational runway estimate.

Files changed (high-level): see files_changed field below for a concise list.

Checklist: - [x] CLI implemented and unit-tested - [x] Telemetry adapter implemented and integration-tested against Optimize staging - [x] Policy templates and validator - [x] Docs and examples - [x] Helm bits for private deploy - [x] Security review (KMS usage for small secrets)

Risks and mitigations: - Risk: overly aggressive quant suggestions could degrade quality. Mitigation: profiles include a quality-safety floor and require an explicit opt-in flag to apply to live model manifests. - Risk: telemetry flooding. Mitigation: adapter performs sampling and pre-aggregation and uses the existing Redact/PII path for sensitive fields.

Related work: builds on ENG-4301 (prefill policy schemas) and reuses portions of the econ-simulator in /tools/sim. Linear references: ENG-4352 (Runway Guardian roadmap), PM-1218 (product acceptance criteria).

review_comments: Diego Morales: Nice end-to-end shape. Please add a short rationale comment in the sim about why we bias toward lower batch sizes for ramping tenants.
Priya Nair: Telemetry adapter looks good but add a flag to toggle sampling rate per-tenant; we don't want one-size-for-all sampling. Also add an opentracing span around normalization.
Alex Kim: Can we make the compact profile tie to model semantic version so downstream can detect incompatible profiles? Otherwise lgtm.
SRE oncall (comment): Helm fragment needs resource requests to avoid OOMs during install; suggest 200m/256Mi baseline.
Security review (Kiran): KMS usage looks fine; ensure the docker image doesn't leak build secrets. Add a pipeline step to scan image for credentials.
QA: e2e_runway smoke failed intermittently due to flakiness in the e2e harness - added retry in the script and extended wait for deployment readiness.
author_responses: Eloise Chen: Added the sim rationale comment and a conservative default batch bias. Added --sampling-rate and per-tenant override flag; opentracing spans inserted. Compact profile now includes model_semver. Helm resources added. Thanks for the reviews!
merge_summary: Squash-merged after approvals from Diego, Priya, and Alex; CI green. 1 review iteration for telemetry sampling and helm resources.
notes_for_release: Introduce Runway Guardian (CLI + telemetry adapter + compact quant generator). Admins should review default templates in docs/runway-guardian.md before enabling in production. CLI is opt-in and safe by default; compact quant profiles require explicit apply to model manifests.
post_merge_actions: Deploy runway-agent Helm chart to staging (infra runbook updated)
Schedule a canary for 48h using tenant sample set A
Follow-up: ENG-4410 to hook Optimize recommendations into Console UI
backports: release/2026.02: small backport of CLI flags and telemetry adapter sampling
egress_implications: Adapter forwards aggregated envelopes to Optimize staging endpoint; uses existing longtail egress ACLs; no new external third-party endpoints.
security_notes: KMS integration for short-lived adapter credentials; profiles include explicit opt-in. No secrets committed. Image scanned during CI.
operational_docs: docs/runway-guardian.md and docs/runway-guardian-examples.md include install, config, and post-deploy checklist to validate runway estimates.
test_plan: Unit tests cover generator logic and serializer. Integration tests exercise telemetry adapter + Optimize staging (mock). e2e smoke deploy in helm/regression CI. Manual QA run with tenant sample A.
regression_risks: Modest: sim affects only CLI outputs, not live serving behavior. Telemetry adapter sits in parallel to existing ingest path and samples aggressively by default in staging only.
changelog_entry: Added Runway Guardian CLI and telemetry adapter for conservative prefill defaults and compact quant profile emission. (opt-in)
